solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Plant holding partition down (7)

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

blocks.note: to sow is to plant seed
a wall partitions a space

annotation.surface: A gardener's note about a plant clinging to a fallen partition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction or feathers, but here it is the verb: to down a drink is to swallow it.
annotation.definitionFit: To down something, like a pint, is to swallow it.

entries.clue: Salomé’s opening nearby, it could be in the round (6)

annotation.definition: it could be in the round

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Salomé
handy = close at hand

annotation.surface: Salomé dancing nearby, perhaps in a theatre in the round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the round' suggests staging, but a round here is drinks bought for the group; a shandy is beer mixed with lemonade.
annotation.definitionFit: A shandy is a drink one might order as part of a round at the pub.

entries.clue: Social cycling doesn’t involve national sports team (3,6)

indicators.note: the first letter is moved round to the end

blocks.note: a ball is a social dance
lacks = is without

annotation.surface: A social cycling club that has nothing to do with the national team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social' as a noun is a party or dance. The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby union team, named for their black kit.
annotation.definitionFit: The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby team.

entries.clue: Launching activity to influence legislators with years to go (7)

indicators.note: the named letter is to go, i.e. be removed

blocks.note: lobbying is pressing legislators for a cause
y = years; this Y is removed

annotation.surface: A campaign launch aimed at swaying legislators, with years still to run.
annotation.walkthrough: Remove Y from LOBBYING. 'Launching' reads as starting a campaign, but it means throwing: to lob is to toss high.
annotation.definitionFit: Lobbing a ball is launching it in a high arc.

entries.clue: Brag about compound in Midlands city (9)

indicators.note: 'about' as in 'about turn': the word faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: to crow is to brag
an ester is a chemical compound

annotation.surface: Someone boasting about a chemical works in a Midlands city.
annotation.walkthrough: Worcester is a cathedral city in the English West Midlands, home of Worcestershire sauce.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain geographical fact: Worcester stands on the River Severn in the West Midlands region of England.

entries.clue: Company note port is full of spirit (3,4)

blocks.note: co = company
NB, nota bene, is a written note
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port

annotation.surface: A company memo announcing the port wine is fortified with spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' tempts a musical letter, but it is NB, the 'take note' written in margins. Con brio is a musical direction: play with vigour.
annotation.definitionFit: Con brio is Italian for 'with vigour', i.e. full of spirit.

entries.clue: Tomb Raider: you play at first in skin of Croft (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of these words
the first letters go inside the other piece
a word's skin is its outer letters

blocks.note: first of the outer letters of Croft
first letters of Raider, you, play
last of the outer letters of Croft

annotation.surface: An invitation to play the video game Tomb Raider as its heroine, Lara Croft.
annotation.walkthrough: The title Tomb Raider is split: 'Tomb' is the definition while 'Raider' gives only its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground tomb, often beneath a church.

entries.clue: Ban goes awry where muzzle may be covered (7)

indicators.note: the letters go awry, out of their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A muzzle ban has gone wrong, leaving the question of where muzzles are allowed.
annotation.walkthrough: The muzzle here is a horse's snout rather than a dog's restraint; a nosebag is the feed bag hung over it.
annotation.definitionFit: A nosebag is hung over a horse's muzzle to hold its feed.

entries.clue: Therapy that’s more pointed without special backing (5)

indicators.note: the named letters are left out
in a down clue, backing sends the letters upwards, i.e. backwards

blocks.note: spikier = more pointed
sp = special; these letters are removed

annotation.surface: A treatment described as sharper when it lacks special support.
annotation.walkthrough: SPIKIER without SP leaves IKIER, which runs backwards. Reiki is a Japanese healing practice done by laying on hands.
annotation.definitionFit: Reiki is an alternative therapy using touch.

entries.clue: Running amok with Halo, OK? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: OK is the postal abbreviation for Oklahoma

indicators.note: the letters run about into a new order

blocks.note: part of the anagram fodder
rest of the anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Someone asking if it's all right to run wild in the video game Halo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'OK?' reads as asking permission, but OK is the US state abbreviation. The question mark flags this definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: OK is the standard two-letter abbreviation for the US state of Oklahoma.

entries.clue: Tribal yet unusually free (2,7)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged unusually

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A tribal people who are nonetheless strangely free.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word; the surface's contrast of tribal and free is only decoration around a straight anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone at liberty is not confined, i.e. free, as an escaped prisoner is.

entries.clue: Where drinks are made without added carbon dioxide (5)

blocks.note: the apparatus in which spirits are distilled
describes water or lemonade with no fizz

annotation.surface: A description of a place where uncarbonated drinks are produced.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one definition of a soft-drinks plant; it splits into a distilling apparatus and a word for non-sparkling.
annotation.definitionFit: A still is where spirits are distilled; still drinks lack fizz.

entries.clue: City kept changing sides before international (5)

indicators.note: the letters at the two sides of the word swap places
the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: held = kept; H and D swap ends to make DELH
i = international

annotation.surface: A city that kept switching allegiance before going international.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changing sides' sounds like defecting, but it swaps the outer letters: HELD becomes DELH.
annotation.definitionFit: Delhi is a major city in India, containing the capital New Delhi.

entries.clue: Go into the Spanish sort of institute (9)

indicators.note: the first piece goes into the second

blocks.note: el = 'the' in Spanish; first letter of the pair around STAB
to have a go is to have a stab
the second letter of EL
-ish = sort of

annotation.surface: Someone joining a Spanish institute of some kind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Institute' reads as a noun, but here it is the verb: to institute something is to establish it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to institute a rule or custom is to set it up.

entries.clue: Drunk groom got us ice as proof of life? (6,4,3)

indicators.note: the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A tipsy bridegroom fetched ice for the party, somehow proving he was alive.
annotation.walkthrough: Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am' offers the fact of thinking as proof that one exists; the question mark marks the playful definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Descartes' cogito argues that thinking proves one's own existence.

entries.clue: Swiss production cast Hamlet around king and queen, say (9)

indicators.note: the letters are cast into a new arrangement
the rearranged letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: HAMLET rearranged, split around MEN
king and queen are chess men

annotation.surface: A Swiss theatre production casting Hamlet alongside a king and queen.
annotation.walkthrough: The Hamlet setting makes king and queen look like roles, but they are pieces, i.e. chessmen.
annotation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a cheese produced in Switzerland.

entries.clue: Increase appeal of cold Italian sauces, recalled on the way up (5-4)

indicators.note: called back, i.e. running backwards
in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second
in a down clue, up means written backwards

blocks.note: c = cold, as on a tap
ragù is an Italian meat sauce
the Tao is 'the way' in Chinese philosophy

annotation.surface: A cook reheating cold pasta sauces on the way up to boost their appeal.
annotation.walkthrough: Both parts are read upwards in this down clue. 'The way' is a Chinese philosophical term, not a road, which is why it is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: To sugar-coat something is to make it more appealing.

entries.clue: Instantly appreciate formal headwear when out of work (4,4)

indicators.note: the named letters are taken out

blocks.note: to like = to appreciate
a top hat; OP is removed to leave THAT
op = opus, a work; removed

annotation.surface: Someone instantly taking to formal hats once they are unemployed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of work' reads as jobless, but it says OP comes out of TOPHAT. 'Just like that' means instantly, with a snap of the fingers.
annotation.definitionFit: Done 'like that' (with a snap of the fingers) means instantly.

entries.clue: Sharing on social media popular with men only? Smashing! (13)

indicators.note: the pieces are placed together

blocks.note: in = popular, fashionable
a stag party is for men only
ramming = smashing into

annotation.surface: A cheer for a social media post that went down well at a men-only party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smashing!' reads as British praise meaning great, but it is RAMMING, crashing into things. A stag night is a groom's men-only party.
annotation.definitionFit: Instagramming is posting photos to the Instagram social media app.

entries.clue: Where you shouldn’t pull with difficulty? (2,1,4)

blocks.note: at a door marked PUSH, pulling is wrong
British idiom for 'only just, if pressed'

annotation.surface: Advice on doors that you shouldn't struggle to pull open.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: at a door signed PUSH you shouldn't pull. 'At a push' is British for 'if really necessary, with effort'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done at a push is managed only with difficulty.

entries.clue: British playwright dismissing top writer’s acting (7)

indicators.note: the top (first) letter is dismissed

blocks.note: Harold Pinter; losing its top letter P gives INTER
the writer's = I'm, 'I am', the setter speaking

annotation.surface: A British playwright is fired from the top writing job while still acting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Acting' suggests the stage, fitting a playwright, but it means temporary, as in an acting manager.
annotation.definitionFit: An acting head is an interim one, filling in temporarily.

entries.clue: Get very tired after knocking out American amongst the best at Wimbledon? (6)

indicators.note: the named letter is knocked out

blocks.note: to get a point is to see it
dead = exhausted, as in dead on one's feet
a = American; knocked out of DEAD to leave DED

annotation.surface: A tennis player worn out after beating an American opponent among Wimbledon's elite.
annotation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; the best players are seeded so they avoid each other early. 'Knocking out' sounds like a tennis win, but it removes A.
annotation.definitionFit: Seeded players are ranked among the best in a tournament draw.

entries.clue: Emigrant touring island next to Iona, not quite making amends (9)

indicators.note: goes round the next piece
the pieces sit side by side
the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an expat lives abroad; goes round I
i = island
Iona minus its last letter

annotation.surface: An emigrant visits islands beside Iona, the Scottish holy isle, on a pilgrimage of repentance.
annotation.walkthrough: Iona is a Scottish island famed as an early Christian site, which makes the penitent surface fit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a religious flavour: to expiate a sin is to atone for it, making amends.

entries.clue: Chinese native with makings of father? (5)

blocks.note: father = pa; its first building letter
and = with, joining the two letters
the other letter that makes up pa

annotation.surface: A Chinese man who looks like father material.
annotation.walkthrough: The makings of father are the letters of PA; the question mark admits that pandas are being read as would-be dads.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the giant panda is an animal found wild only in the mountains of China.

entries.clue: More distant royal once found beneath here in Versailles (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits below the second

blocks.note: ici is French for 'here'
ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

annotation.surface: A remote former royal discovered at Versailles, beneath the palace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'More distant' reads as further away, but it means cooler in manner. Versailles only signals French.
annotation.definitionFit: An icier person is colder and more distant in manner.

entries.clue: Short characters sitting in booster seat (5)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'booster' into the start of 'seat'

annotation.surface: Small characters perched in a child's booster seat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short characters' pictures small people, but 'Short' is the definition and 'characters' is the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short reply, brief to the point of rudeness, is a curt one.

entries.clue: One’s observant in probing high-definition movie certificate (5)

indicators.note: the first piece probes into the second

blocks.note: HD = high-definition; first letter
in itself, probing HD
second letter of HD
U = universal, the British film rating for all ages

annotation.surface: A sharp-eyed viewer inspecting a film's high-definition release and its certificate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Observant' reads as sharp-eyed, but it means religiously observant: a Hindu is one who observes that faith.
annotation.definitionFit: A Hindu is one who observes the Hindu religion.

entries.clue: Writer originally identifying location for Robin Hood (9)

indicators.note: take the original, first letter

blocks.note: first letter of identifying
Sherwood Forest, Robin Hood's haunt

annotation.surface: A writer who first pinpointed where Robin Hood lived.
annotation.walkthrough: Christopher Isherwood was the English author of Goodbye to Berlin; Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire is Robin Hood's legendary home.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Christopher Isherwood wrote the Berlin stories behind the musical Cabaret.

entries.clue: A head bitten by short seabird’s beak (7)

indicators.note: the first piece is held in the jaws of the second
the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a tern is a seabird; short, it is TER
'a head' = each, as in £5 a head

annotation.surface: A person's head bitten by the short beak of a seabird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is old British school slang for a teacher (also a magistrate), not a bird's bill as the seabird suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang, a beak is a schoolmaster, i.e. a teacher.

entries.clue: Song about Cambridge University lacking in scope (7)

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second

blocks.note: a lied is a German art song
MIT is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

annotation.surface: A song about Cambridge University that falls short in ambition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge University' points to England, but MIT is in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a narrow, restricted plan or mind is one lacking in scope.
